podcast.body: This album was recorded during a period when Trent Reznor was struggling with deep depression and severe addictions to alcohol and drugs like coke and heroin, following the release of "The Downward Spiral." Despite his personal struggles, he managed to complete the album. He later reflected that he "whitetnuckled it through the recording of The Fragile."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This double album reached number one on the charts in October 1999, indicating a significant breakthrough for the band and a continued presence for rock acts amidst rising pop and hip-hop. "But in October, 9-inch nails reach number one with the double album, The Fragile."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The 00's Part 1: The Sad State of Rock

podcast.title: Chart Performance and Relapse
podcast.body: When "The Fragile" album was released, it debuted at number one, leading Trent Reznor to believe he was "cured" of his addiction. This perception initiated a period of a year and a half where he "spent a good year and a half testing to see how low I could go," resulting in a miserable and dangerous tour. "When the record came out, I thought, I am cured. It's debut at number one. It was off to the races again."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Double Album
podcast.body: This long-awaited double album was released in 1999. It represents a later phase in Nine Inch Nails' career, following the success of "The Downward Spiral," and is noted as one of the significant releases in Trent Reznor's well-documented post-platinum period. "And of course, the long-awaited 1999 double album, The Fragile."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This album was also based on a concept and is considered in many ways a sequel to *The Downward Spiral*, exploring themes of everything falling apart and the fear associated with that. However, even Trent Reznor admits that it lacks significant focus. "If you examine it very carefully, it's in many ways a sequel of The Downward Spiral, with its themes of everything falling apart in the fear that comes along with that, but even Trent admits that there's really not much focus to it."

podcast.body: Trent Reznor worked through the recording of this album while secretly dealing with addiction in 1997, believing he had overcome it upon the album's release, only to face a severe relapse afterward. "I kind of whitet-nuckled it through the recording of the fragile and on a pretty slippery slope. And when the record came out, you know, I thought, I am cured."
